content: West Nile virus (WNV) infection is recognized as a clinical spectrum, presenting in one of three distinct forms. Approximately 70-80% of individuals infected with WNV remain asymptomatic. Around 20% of cases manifest as a mild febrile illness known as West Nile fever, while less than 1% of cases progress to a severe neuroinvasive disease, which may present as West Nile meningitis or encephalitis. Patients suspected of having WNV infection should be specifically questioned about recent mosquito bites. Additional historical details that may provide diagnostic clues include the time of year, geographical location, recent travel history, and outdoor activities. It is also essential to inquire about virus-associated symptoms and their progression. Asymptomatic Presentation Approximately 80% of individuals infected with WNV exhibit no symptoms and remain asymptomatic throughout the course of the infection. West Nile Fever West Nile fever is characterized by a range of constitutional, head, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, and cutaneous symptoms: Constitutional Symptoms: Fever, chills, body aches, fatigue, joint pain (arthralgia), excessive sweating (diaphoresis), drowsiness, loss of appetite (anorexia), and insomnia. Head, Eye, Ear, Nose, and Throat (HEENT) Symptoms: Headache, ocular pain, hearing impairment, and cough. Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Genitourinary Symptoms: Bladder urgency and urinary incontinence. Cutaneous Manifestations: Macular or papular skin rash, typically on the trunk, and lymphadenopathy. Neuroinvasive Disease Neuroinvasive disease represents the most severe form of WNV infection. Patients may present with fever accompanied by a variety of neurological manifestations, including flaccid paralysis, symptoms of meningitis or encephalitis, or a combination of these conditions. Constitutional Symptoms: High fever and diffuse body aches. Neurological Symptoms: A wide range of neurological symptoms may occur, including but not limited to flaccid paralysis, altered mental status, seizures, and focal neurological deficits. These symptoms vary in frequency and severity among affected individuals.
